summary: The Nomai were a technologically advanced nomadic species who traveled to the Hearthian solar system following a signal from the Eye of the Universe. Their Vessel crashed in Dark Bramble; they settled the system, attempted to find the Eye via the Ash Twin Project, and were wiped out by Ghost Matter from the Interloper before succeeding.

biology: Nomai are tall, slender, digitigrade beings with three eyes.
Nomai faces closely resemble goats from the Bovidae family or Caprinae subfamily.
Nomai have triple-digit hands and short tails.
Nomai heads are adorned with three antlers: two on each side and one extending from the top in two points.
Nomai have a shockingly fragile bone structure according to the Observatory museum.
Nomai may have originated from a low-gravity world or have lived in zero gravity before developing artificial gravity.
Nomai wear traditional life-support apparatus for protection in the local environment.
behavior: Nomai philosophy holds two tenets: 'Identify and Explain' — to seek out and to understand.
Nomai have a strong preference for non-interference toward lesser-evolved life forms.
Nomai take extreme care when extracting resources from inhabited worlds to avoid disturbing native life.
Nomai display some degree of apparent telekinesis when interacting with technology, demonstrated by Solanum stacking rocks to communicate.
location: Nomai artifacts and structures can be found on all celestial bodies in the solar system.
Nomai first settled on Ember Twin and Brittle Hollow after the Vessel crash.
Surviving modern Nomai clans elsewhere broadcast travel to the Gloaming Galaxy, where stars remain relatively stable.
lore: The Nomai race consists of multiple clans.
Each Nomai clan lives within a Nomai Vessel, a spaceship equipped with an Advanced Warp Core for interstellar exploration.
Every ten years, the Nomai clans meet at a festival to celebrate their species' discoveries.
Each clan sends an envoy to present their discoveries since the last festival.
Most Nomai have names based on plant species.
Idaea's opposition to the Sun Station demonstrated the Nomai preference for non-interference; he argued failure would destroy all life in the solar system.
The Nomai took precautions when mining Timber Hearth so as not to disrupt the primitive prehistoric Hearthians.
The Nomai language is written in curving branches, often with each new branch coming from a different individual.
Nomai write text by 'typing' it on a staff-like sceptre and pressing the opposite end onto a surface.
Nomai text appears on walls, on circular hovering disc displays, on scrolls, tablets, and recording devices.
Some Nomai text is written as if spoken in the moment, possibly via voice-to-text technology.
The traditional Nomai sceptre symbolically functions as a piano for the Protagonist in the ending.
Nomai demonstrated mastery of faster-than-light travel, quantum mechanics, zero-G construction, and time manipulation.
Nomai had the capacity to create and manipulate black holes.
Nomai could build spaceships, travel between galaxies, and at their peak could send information back in time.
Early Nomai history before arrival in the Hearthian solar system is largely unknown.
What little is known about early Nomai history is recorded in the Observatory and in writings spread throughout the solar system.
The Nomai followed a signal from the Eye of the Universe to the Hearthian solar system.
The Eye signal received by the Nomai was only a temporary pulse, caused by the Stranger's signal blocker being briefly disabled by the Prisoner.
The brief signal prevented the Nomai from precisely locating the Eye and stranded them in Dark Bramble.
After the Vessel was disabled, the Nomai built the Sunless City on Ember Twin and the Hanging City on Brittle Hollow.
When their initial Eye Signal Locators on the Attlerock and Brittle Hollow failed, they built more sophisticated machines: the Orbital Probe Cannon, Sun Station, and Ash Twin Project.
The Nomai's plan: induce a supernova via the Sun Station, which would power the Ash Twin Project, which would send probe-launch data back 22 minutes for re-aiming.
Nomai explorers discovered the Interloper after the Sun Station's initial failure and identified its core as highly unstable.
Before the Nomai explorers could warn their kin, the Interloper's core ruptured and released Ghost Matter, killing all Nomai in the solar system instantly.
Remaining Nomai clans elsewhere became aware that universe-wide stars were rapidly going supernova — what they called the imminent death of the Universe.
Surviving Nomai began broadcasting warnings encouraging clans to travel to the Gloaming Galaxy.
The Vessel's Escape Pod 1 carried Filix, Kousa, Plume, and Thatch to Brittle Hollow.
The Vessel's Escape Pod 2 carried Annona, Bur, Coleus, Melorae, and Rhus to Ember Twin.
The Vessel's Escape Pod 3 carried Escall, Din, and Secca; it crashed in Dark Bramble.
Foli and Keek died in the original Vessel crash.
Modern Nomai broadcasting from elsewhere include Bromi, Canna, Clem, Hyssop, and Neem.
mechanics: Nomai navigation signs on Brittle Hollow can self-correct after being knocked over, indicating their telekinesis-like interactions are technological rather than innate.
